points.description: States that a char [] (C-style character array / C-string) automatically has a null character ('\0', the null terminator) added at the end of the string when the input is read into it.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the student says a terminating/end character is added to char [] but does not identify it precisely as the null character '\0'.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes from the string type: a variable of type string (the string class) does not require or show a null terminator added by the user/at the end of the data; it is not a null-terminated char array. The contrast must be explicit.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the contrast is stated only vaguely, e.g. string handles its ending differently, without saying no null terminator is added.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact: char [] automatically gets a null character ('\0') appended at the end, with an explicit contrast that type string does not. Vague answers such as "char [] is an array" or "string is easier to use" earn nothing. Any wrong statement about the null character, such as saying string adds it and char [] does not, loses the affected point.
